regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Dabrafenib and trametinib for advanced BRAF-mutated melanoma
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Dabrafenib and trametinib block two points in a growth pathway used by BRAF V600-mutated melanoma. In this advanced-disease setting the aim is disease control, with the effect on symptoms, side effects and your priorities reviewed regularly.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: NCCP 00415a: unresectable or metastatic melanoma with a BRAF V600 mutation. This route covers advanced disease; the separate 00415/adjuvant guide covers the 12-month postoperative setting. Separate 00415b postoperative stage III BRAF V600 setting: planned 12 months, with its own patient route and consent discussion.
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: A BRAF V600 change can keep the cell-growth pathway switched on. Dabrafenib blocks the altered BRAF protein. It is paired with a MEK inhibitor to act on the same pathway at another point. The BRAF result comes from tumour testing; it does not automatically mean a hereditary condition. MEK carries growth signals further along the pathway below BRAF. Trametinib blocks MEK alongside dabrafenib. Normal heart, eye, lung and other tissues can also be affected, which is why scheduled tests and prompt symptom reporting matter.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Take dabrafenib twice daily, around 12 hours apart, and trametinib once daily. Both are taken every day unless the team instructs a hold. Treatment for advanced melanoma continues while beneficial and tolerable; there is no preset cycle total. A 28-day calendar is a review period, not a treatment-free week. For the separate adjuvant route, treatment is planned for 12 months; do not transfer the advanced-disease endpoint.
key_points: Advanced and adjuvant treatment are distinct; do not apply a 12-month endpoint to all patients.
Fever holds both drugs; other toxicities may have component-specific rules. The treating team decides restart and dose changes.

regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Nivolumab and ipilimumab help immune cells recognise and attack melanoma. The combination phase is followed by nivolumab alone when appropriate. The aim in this setting is to control advanced disease; benefit and toxicity are reviewed for the individual.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: NCCP 00431a: advanced unresectable or metastatic melanoma in adults. This patient guide is the melanoma context, not the separate liver-cancer indication.
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Nivolumab blocks PD-1, a signal that can reduce T-cell activity. This can help immune cells act against melanoma, but it can also allow inflammation in healthy organs. It is not conventional chemotherapy and side effects can occur even after doses have stopped. Ipilimumab blocks CTLA-4, another checkpoint involved in controlling T cells. Combining it with nivolumab increases immune activity and can increase immune-related toxicity. The four-dose combination phase has a different treatment plan from nivolumab maintenance.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: The combination phase gives nivolumab followed by ipilimumab by IV infusion every three weeks for up to four doses. If appropriate, nivolumab alone then continues on the team-selected two-weekly or four-weekly schedule, by the prescribed IV or subcutaneous route. After the last combination dose, the first two-weekly maintenance dose starts three weeks later; the first four-weekly maintenance dose starts six weeks later in this melanoma schedule. Treatment continues until progression or unacceptable toxicity, subject to review.

Four induction doses do not mean the whole treatment course is four doses.
Prior immune toxicity and permanent-stop decisions remain relevant when maintenance starts.

administration.cycle_and_sequence: The combination phase gives nivolumab followed by ipilimumab by IV infusion every three weeks for up to four doses. If appropriate, nivolumab alone then continues on the team-selected two-weekly or four-weekly schedule, by the prescribed IV or subcutaneous route. After the last combination dose, the first two-weekly maintenance dose starts three weeks later; the first four-weekly maintenance dose starts six weeks later in this melanoma schedule. Treatment continues until progression or unacceptable toxicity, subject to review.
route_and_duration: At each combination visit, nivolumab is given before ipilimumab, as separate IV infusions. The source schedule gives each over 30 minutes; allow extra time for assessment, preparation and observation. regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Lung cancer only: first-line metastatic NSCLC or adjuvant NSCLC after surgery and platinum chemotherapy
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: PD-1 blockade restores antitumour T-cell activity. First-line metastatic and post-resection adjuvant NSCLC have separate populations, treatment goals and evidence; the shared protocol does not make their eligibility interchangeable.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Lung cancer only: first-line metastatic NSCLC or adjuvant NSCLC after surgery and platinum chemotherapy
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Pembrolizumab: Pembrolizumab is an antibody that blocks PD-1, a control switch on immune T cells. Cancer cells can use this switch to reduce immune attack. Blocking it can help the immune system recognise and attack cancer. The same increased immune activity can inflame healthy organs, which is why new symptoms need attention even after treatment ends.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Pembrolizumab 200 mg is given as a drip over about 30 minutes on Day 1 every 3 weeks (21 days). The hospital visit is longer because of checks and preparation. After complete surgery and platinum chemotherapy, the adjuvant course lasts up to 12 months. For metastatic cancer, treatment continues while it remains helpful and tolerable; the team may consider stopping after 24 months of sustained response without progression, or continuing when appropriate.
key_points: Minimal emetic risk; no usual routine premedication.
No pembrolizumab dose reduction; apply specific hold/permanent-stop and restart criteria.
Grade 4/recurrent grade3 generic immune rules have specific endocrine exceptions; controlled hypothyroidism need not interrupt treatment.
Creatinine is ×ULN, never ×baseline; hepatitis and nephritis thresholds must not be confused with stable organ impairment recommendations.
Every-3–6-week thyroid checks continue on both infusion schedules.
Shared clinical protocol; new patient suite is lung-only.

Abnormal liver tests or creatinine do not establish immune causality. Record clinician-assessed hepatitis/nephritis before the definitive source hold/stop pathway; unexplained abnormalities remain a clinical-review decision.

KEYNOTE-091 final OS analysis at ESMO 2026 did not demonstrate a statistically significant OS improvement; chemotherapy-subgroup DFS figures are updated and labelled separately from metastatic KEYNOTE-024.

Requested restart needs documented source-specific recovery, required steroid management/taper and consultant confirmation. Table 1 endocrine exceptions remain separate; existing 12-week failure/taper and permanent-stop criteria retain priority.

treatment_rationale.summary: PD-1 blockade restores antitumour T-cell activity. First-line metastatic and post-resection adjuvant NSCLC have separate populations, treatment goals and evidence; the shared protocol does not make their eligibility interchangeable.
treatment_rationale.setting: Lung cancer only: first-line metastatic NSCLC or adjuvant NSCLC after surgery and platinum chemotherapy
treatment_rationale.line: First-line metastatic OR post-resection adjuvant after platinum chemotherapy
factors: Confirm the exact lung indication and treatment aim. Metastatic first-line: validated PD-L1 TPS ≥50%, no EGFR mutation or ALK translocation, stage IV, no prior systemic metastatic treatment, ECOG 0–1.

Adjuvant: complete resection, prior platinum chemotherapy, high recurrence-risk/pathological stage IB–IIIA AJCC7 source criteria, ECOG 0–1; confirm reimbursement/access separately. No metastatic TPS50 eligibility requirement applies.

FBC, renal and liver profiles, glucose and thyroid function. Review autoimmune disease, prior interstitial lung disease, infection, untreated brain metastases, steroid/immunosuppressive use, prior checkpoint treatment, pregnancy/breastfeeding and medicines.
alternatives: Choose among available systemic, targeted, clinical-trial, surveillance and supportive-care options using the precise setting, biomarkers, comorbidity and patient preferences.
limitations: These lung trials used pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks. Trial treatment limits and research scan schedules are not automatic NCCP prescribing rules.

KEYNOTE-024: selected untreated metastatic TPS≥50%, no sensitising EGFR/ALK; 66% effective crossover to subsequent PD-1/PD-L1 therapy in the chemotherapy group. Results are not for the adjuvant setting.

key_findings: Median PFS: combination 11.5 months (95%CI 8.9–16.7), ipilimumab 2.9 months (2.8–3.4), nivolumab 6.9 months (4.3–9.5).

Grade 3–4 treatment-related adverse events at this analysis:55.0% combination,16.3% nivolumab,27.3% ipilimumab.
limitations: The planned statistical comparisons were against ipilimumab; a superiority claim over nivolumab alone is not supported by a powered direct comparison.

evidence_records.publication_title: Efficacy and Safety of Vismodegib in Advanced Basal-Cell Carcinoma
evidence_records.evidence_relationship: Pivotal single-arm trial with separately labelled follow-up analyses
evidence_records.evidence_context: Advanced basal cell carcinoma: metastatic and locally advanced cohorts; interpret against the exact NCCP adult indication.
evidence_records.study_design: International, multicentre, open-label phase II study with two nonrandomised cohorts and no control arm.
evidence_records.trial_population: 104 patients treated: 33 metastatic and 71 locally advanced BCC. Efficacy analyses included 33 metastatic and 63 locally advanced cases after independent pathology review. Adults had ECOG 0-2 and adequate organ function; locally advanced disease was inoperable or surgery was inappropriate, with radiotherapy previously unsuccessful, contraindicated or inappropriate.
evidence_records.intervention: Vismodegib 150 mg orally once daily until progression, unacceptable toxicity or withdrawal.
evidence_records.comparator: None. The primary analysis tested ORR against prespecified null rates of 10% for metastatic and 20% for locally advanced BCC; these thresholds are not a treatment-control group.
evidence_records.primary_endpoint: Independently assessed, confirmed objective response (complete or partial). Metastatic BCC used RECIST 1.0. Locally advanced BCC used a composite of external/radiographic lesion reduction or ulceration resolution without progression, with biopsy contributing to complete-response classification; response confirmation required at least four weeks.
evidence_records.relevance_summary: Supports tumour-response activity in eligible advanced BCC. The current EMA summary reports an independent-review update 21 months after the final enrolment and a distinct investigator-assessed analysis 39 months after final enrolment.
evidence_records.match_type: Same drug and advanced BCC disease settings; maintain the exact NCCP eligibility criteria and do not extrapolate these response rates to routine resectable BCC.
key_findings: Primary analysis, November 2010 (9 months after the last enrolment), independent review: 10/33 metastatic cases responded (30.3%, reported as 30% in the original paper); 27/63 locally advanced cases responded (42.9%, reported as 43%). Median response duration was 7.6 months in each cohort.

EMA Table 2 independent-review analysis, 21 months after the last enrolment (the 12-month update of the primary analysis): metastatic ORR 11/33, 33.3% (95% CI 19.2-51.8%); locally advanced ORR 30/63, 47.6% (95% CI 35.5-60.6%).
At that same 21-month independent-review analysis, median response duration was 7.6 months in metastatic and 9.5 months in locally advanced BCC; complete responses were 0/33 and 14/63, respectively.

Later 39-month analysis after the last enrolment used investigator assessment: metastatic ORR 16/33, 48.5% (95% CI 30.8-66.2%); locally advanced ORR 38/63, 60.3% (95% CI 47.2-71.7%). These are not independent-review results.
At the 39-month investigator analysis, median response duration was 14.8 and 26.2 months, respectively. These descriptive durations do not establish superiority over another treatment.
evidence_records.limitations: Single-arm evidence with no randomised comparator cannot establish a comparative survival benefit or cure rate. The two cohorts used different response assessments and must remain separate. Analyses use 96 efficacy-evaluable patients, rather than all 104 treated patients; eight locally advanced cases were excluded after independent pathology review. The small cohorts, selected ECOG 0-2 population and entirely White study population limit generalisability. Longer follow-up and investigator review do not make the later percentages interchangeable with the independent primary endpoint.
evidence_records.review_status: Primary and regulatory source reconciliation complete; independent clinical and pharmacy review pending
